summary: walkGraph buildScopeFilter startIndex=1 collides with $1 chunkIds; LIMIT binds to text[]
description:
Live error: 'argument of LIMIT must be type bigint, not type text[]' (Postgres 42804) on POST /api/query.

Bug in src/lib/graph.ts walkGraph: buildScopeFilter is called with startIndex=1, but $1 is already used by 'WHERE id = ANY($1::text[])'. Two failure modes:

  - Empty scope prefs: paramIndex stays 1, so 'LIMIT $1' binds to chunkIds (text[]).
  - Non-empty scope prefs: scope clauses use $1 (collides with chunkIds), and the params array shifts so a text[] (blocked traditions, etc.) lands in the LIMIT slot.

Pre-existing since 4f210bc (2026-04-17) but masked previously — likely because extractConcepts returned no concepts on common queries, or queries failed earlier in the pipeline. Surfaced now that the v2 corpus deploy unblocked the rest of the retrieval path.

Fix: startIndex should be 2 (because $1 is the chunkIds slot). vectorSearch already does this correctly. Add a regression test that exercises walkGraph with both empty and non-empty scope prefs.

Done when:
- graph.ts walkGraph passes 2 to buildScopeFilter
- regression test in src/__tests__/graph.test.ts covers empty + non-empty scope prefs and asserts the SQL params land in the right slots
- POST /api/query no longer 500s in prod

resolution.note: buildScopeFilter(prefs, 2) — $1 reserved for chunkIds. Regression test covers empty + blacklist + whitelist scope prefs.
